title: Technical Drawing Generator — Overview and definition
t: Technical Drawing Generator — Overview and definition
description: Turns 3D models into standards-compliant 2D engineering drawings with views, dimensions, and annotations.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Turns 3D models into standards-compliant 2D engineering drawings with views, dimensions, and annotations. A technical drawing generator projects 3D geometry into orthographic, section, detail, and auxiliary views, places dimensions and geometric tolerances per ASME Y14.5 or ISO 128, and produces title blocks, revision tables, and bills of materials. Real implementations use hidden-line removal, tangent-edge handling, and view alignment constraints. Public examples include the TechDraw workbench in FreeCAD and drawing modules in LibreCAD and SolveSpace.
capabilities: Generate front, top, side, section, and detail views from a 3D model
Place linear, angular, radial, and ordinate dimensions with tolerance zones
Apply GD&T symbols, surface finish marks, and weld symbols
Produce title blocks, revision history, and parts lists automatically
Export print-ready vector drawings and check them against drafting standards

body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Data contracts for Technical Drawing Generator. Inputs: A 3D solid or surface model plus a drawing template (sheet size, projection standard, title block). Outputs: A 2D drawing: projected views, dimensions, annotations, and a printable vector file. Accepted input formats: STEP AP203/AP214, IGES, STL, native CAD parts and assemblies. Produced output formats: PDF, SVG, DXF, DWG, PostScript for print.

Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (Generate front, top, side, section, and detail views from a 3D model). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: Generate front, top, side, section, and detail views from a 3D model and Place linear, angular, radial, and ordinate dimensions with tolerance zones. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (2D Computer-Aided Design (CAD) program) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
